author: Electricks94
body: #### PR description: At the moment the view corresponding to a global index is determined by the SoAConstMultiView through a runtime index. Typically the SoAConstMultiView is passed by value to a kernel. This is a problem because kernel parameters live in constant space, and the compiler can only read them directly when the offset is a compile-time constant. If the access is runtime-indexed, it cant address the parameter that way. Instead it materializes the whole struct in a local stack frame, copies everything into it, and indexes that copy. The copy is also not guarded by if (i < view.size()). The stores are emitted at kernel entry, so every thread pays for them, even the ones that exit immediately. Since views can be realativly large the copy with sizeof(SoAConstMultiView) can become a dominating bottleneck. It also adds local-memory traffic that competes with real loads in L1. A template recursion solves this problem, every access is views_[I] and offsets_[I] with a constant I. After inlining, nothing is dynamically indexed, so the struct is split and read straight from param space with constant offsets. The data-dependent part is only the branches, which cost far less than the copy. Divergence is limited to warps that straddle a view boundary. The warp divergence is expected to not matter since the MultiView is meant for larger and few collections. [__grid_constant__](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/cpp-language-extensions.html#grid-constant-parameters) lets the compiler take the address of the parameter instead of copying it, so a dynamic index becomes an indexed constant-bank load. This would be another way to solve the issue but users would need to provide this parameter which is not a solution in our case The performance gain is shown with a small SaxPy benchmark on about 4M elements which are either managed by a single view or split into more and more fragments which are then managed by the SoAConstMultiView **SoAConstMultiView with runtime index to determine the local view** **SoAConstMultiView with compile time index to determine the local view** #### PR validation: PR is validated with checking unit tests locally FYI @felicepantaleo @mmarriot
title: Fix overhead of SoAConstMultiView through compile time indexing
